event.description: Reduce the shared latent width from d=16 to d=14 while retaining two untied two-head blocks, learned positions, and ff=20.
event.proposal: Family: attention organization. Retained incumbent is 4288 parameters at 99.910000%, a +0.910000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: no prior accepted or failed result; 0 prior attempts. The nearest scalar-pruning boundary ff=16 was an optimization failure (validation peaked at 11.4% after 30000 steps), and full-block parameter tying likewise failed (peak 9.7%), but neither tests per-head latent dimensionality. Hypothesis: reducing d_model from 16 to 14 while retaining two heads changes each head from 8 to 7 channels and may preserve the separate attention pathways while removing 760 parameters, from 4288 to 3528. This is a parameterization-preserving latent-width compression, not a representational substitution. It is more informative than the nearest untested alternative d=12 because d=14 supplies the smallest valid two-head decrement and locates the next attention-capacity boundary.
